title: Improving AI Discernment: do misinformation interventions help people spot AI-generated media?

registration.note: AsPredicted #151,281, registered 2023-11-15 (amends #151208). Some data had been collected at registration; batches 3-4 followed the plan.

descriptions.0: No intervention; the respondent proceeds directly to the discernment task.
descriptions.1: Posts in the feed are flagged as potentially AI-generated.
descriptions.2: Posts carry information about the content's source and origin (provenance).
descriptions.3: Posts carry machine-learning-based AI-detection labels (automated flagging).
descriptions.4: Before the feed, an interactive task asks 'Is this image AI-generated?' (accuracy nudge).
descriptions.5: Before the feed, a box-breathing exercise to reduce emotional reactivity.
descriptions.6: Before the feed, a short mindfulness exercise.
descriptions.7: Before the feed, an inoculation message pre-exposing the respondent to manipulation techniques used in AI-generated media.
descriptions.8: Before the feed, an infographic on how to identify AI-generated content.
descriptions.9: Before the feed, an alternative infographic on how to identify AI-generated content.
descriptions.10: Before the feed, a comprehensive guide with examples of AI artifacts in images and videos.
descriptions.11: Before the feed, an educational video about AI-generated text.

derived.ai_scale: (chatgpt + bing + claude + character + dalle + midjourney + stable_diff) / 7

addenda.label: Unadjusted, unweighted difference in means, pooled and per arm
addenda.rationale: The reviewer suspects covariate adjustment (Lin model) or IPW weights drive the gap between the Breathing Exercise estimate and its raw mean difference. Re-fitting as a plain unweighted difference in means with no covariates shows raw estimates that can be reconciled with the adjusted ones.
addenda.expected: If the unadjusted pooled and Breathing Exercise estimates match the raw means (about -0.04 for Breathing Exercise) and the pooled effect is near zero, the registered result depends on the adjustment or weights and should be read cautiously. If they are similar to the adjusted ones, the result is robust.
addenda.issue: The pooled estimate of -0.11 (p=.026) is called 'a small shift', yet no individual arm besides Breathing Exercise differs from zero. The Breathing Exercise estimate (-0.54) is larger than its own arm mean difference (4.146 vs 4.187 = -0.04), which suggests covariate adjustment or weighting drives it. The raw means and the adjusted estimates are not reconciled anywhere.

addenda.label: unadjusted, unweighted difference in means for all arms vs control
addenda.rationale: The reviewer worries the significant H1 effects depend on the IPW weights and covariate interactions. An unweighted, covariate-free difference in means shows the raw effects and whether the weights drive the results.
addenda.expected: Reassuring if raw estimates match the adjusted ones in sign and rough size. Worrying if they are near zero, as the raw means suggest, because that would mean the weights or interactions drive the results.
addenda.issue: The mean_arm values in the CSVs do not match the estimates. Mindfulness is -3.9 points adjusted but its raw arm mean is higher than control (0.696 vs 0.693), and the Guide's raw difference is only 0.6 points against an adjusted +4.7. The significant H1 results therefore depend on the weighted, covariate-interacted model.
